source_text.why-this-recheck-exists: REQ-009 passed your gate at step-02 as part of REQ-007..REQ-032. It has since been AMENDED by ORCH in commit 61a7861. A requirement that changes after passing a gate has not been gated in its current form — that is the whole reason this step exists rather than the amendment standing on ORCH's own say-so.
source_text.who-decided-and-why: The project owner stated on 2026-09-06 that they have no software development background and delegated all unresolved technical decisions to ORCH as the professional. ORCH therefore wrote decisions/0004 (grammY), 0005 (Drizzle ORM + Drizzle Kit) and 0006 (Vitest), and reduced REQ-009's scope from WRITING those three records to IMPLEMENTING them. This delegation is real and recorded, but it is not a reason to relax the gate — an unreviewed decision made under delegation is exactly the kind that needs an independent check.

task.description:
Re-gate the AMENDED REQ-009, and check the three new decision records it now depends on, per WF-01 Step 2.

START FROM THE DIFF: `git show 61a7861` is the complete change. It touches docs/agents/requirements.yaml (REQ-009 only), docs/agents/AGENT_SYSTEM.md §7, and adds decisions/0004, 0005, 0006.

PART 1 — RE-RUN CHECKS (a)-(e) ON THE AMENDED REQ-009. It is a different requirement than the one you passed: its title changed, its description now cites three decision records instead of mandating them, one acceptance criterion was replaced and one added (6 total, previously 5). Specifically verify:
  - (a) TESTABILITY of the two changed/new criteria. The dependency-pinning criterion says an exact version with no `^` or `~`, and names forbidden alternatives — is that definitively checkable? The CI criterion requires pushing a deliberately failing test on a scratch branch and reading the actual red run before reverting — is that a runnable procedure, or does it describe something an agent cannot actually do in this repo's CI setup? A criterion that cannot be executed is a check-(a) FAIL even if it sounds rigorous.
  - (b) CONSISTENCY with decisions/0003 (which left these three open — confirm 0004/0005/0006 genuinely fill that gap rather than contradicting anything 0003 decided, particularly its TypeScript/Node and apps/bot layout commitments) and with the now-amended AGENT_SYSTEM.md §7.
  - (e) SIZE — the amendment REMOVED work (three records no longer written) and ADDED work (a CI change, verified by a real red run). Net, does REQ-009 still fit one agent turn?

PART 2 — GATE THE THREE DECISION RECORDS THEMSELVES. They were written by ORCH without an independent check; you are it. For each of 0004, 0005, 0006 verify:
  1. It names at least two options with a fair characterization of each — a record that strawmans the rejected option is not a decision, it is a justification. Attack this specifically: 0005 rejects Prisma, whose migration guardrails are genuinely better; 0006 rejects node:test, which has real advantages. Does each record state the cost of its own choice honestly, or does it only argue one side?
  2. Its rationale rests on THIS project's actual stated constraints (PRD §1/§11, core-directives.md) rather than on general industry preference. A rationale that would read identically for any project is weak grounds for a binding record.
  3. It does not contradict a `done` requirement (REQ-001a..REQ-006), decisions/0001-0003, or security-invariants.md.
  4. Its factual claims about the libraries are plausible and not overstated. You have web access — spot-check the load-bearing ones. Two specifically worth testing: 0004's claim that grammY's conversations plugin fits FR-3's restart-safe partial-write requirement (does the plugin actually provide that, or does it merely manage dialogue state in memory, which would NOT satisfy 'a restart mid-form loses nothing'?), and 0006's claim that Vitest's fake timers make the T-24h/T-3h/T+2h logic testable. If either claim is overstated, that is a MAJOR finding — the rationale would be resting on a capability that does not exist as described.

PART 3 — CONSEQUENTIAL CORRECTNESS. 0004 binds all later bot work to keeping domain logic in framework-free modules; 0005 requires SQL review of generated migrations plus SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off under S13 for destructive ones; 0006 changes what TEST-DESIGNER and TEST-RUNNER produce from REQ-010 onward. Are those consequences actually reflected where they need to be — in REQ-009's text, in AGENT_SYSTEM.md, or in the records themselves — or are they stated in a record that nothing else points at? A consequence recorded nowhere the acting agent will read it has not been established.

FAIL on any check failing, naming the requirement or record and the specific problem. If the decisions are sound but a consequence is unwired, that is a MINOR or MAJOR issue rather than a FAIL of the decision itself — say which and why.
acceptance_criteria: Checks (a)-(e) were re-run against the amended REQ-009 in its current form, not carried over from the step-02 verdict.
Both changed/new acceptance criteria were assessed for whether an agent can actually execute them in this repo, with the CI-red-run criterion specifically judged runnable or not.

Each of decisions/0004, 0005 and 0006 was checked for fair option characterization, honest statement of its own choice's cost, and grounding in this project's stated constraints rather than general preference.

The two named library-capability claims (grammY conversations vs FR-3's restart-safe partial writes; Vitest fake timers vs the clock-dependent jobs) were spot-checked against real sources, with the finding stated either way.
Each record was checked against decisions/0001-0003, the done requirements, and security-invariants.md for contradiction.
Every consequence the three records impose on later work was traced to a place an acting agent will actually encounter it, or flagged as unwired.
The verdict states positively what was verified; any FAIL names the specific record or requirement and the problem.

result.summary:
PASS with 4 MINOR issues and 0 MAJOR.

PART 1 - checks (a)-(e) re-run against the amended REQ-009 in its current form.
(a) TESTABILITY - both changed/new criteria pass. The pinning criterion is mechanically checkable: every version string in apps/bot/package.json and the root package.json must start with a digit (no ^ or ~), and the forbidden set is name-matchable (telegraf, prisma, jest, and the four named grammY plugins). The CI-red-run criterion is RUNNABLE in this repo - verified, not assumed: .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml triggers on push to branches ['**'], gh CLI is authenticated against aiqadam/aiqadam-next, and gh run list / gh run view --log-failed return real data. An agent can push a scratch branch, read the actual red run, and revert. deploy-qa and deploy-prod are gated on master / workflow_dispatch, so a scratch branch exercises only the build job - which is the job the criterion is about.
(b) CONSISTENCY - 0004/0005/0006 fill exactly the three gaps that 0003's 'What this record does not decide' left open, and contradict none of 0003's commitments: TypeScript/Node is preserved (all three are Node tooling), and the apps/web + apps/bot layout is preserved (0005 puts migrations under apps/bot/, 0006 puts Vitest at the root covering both workspaces, which is a monorepo-level choice 0003 neither made nor forbade). AGENT_SYSTEM.md section 7's amended entry correctly strikes the closed gap rather than deleting it - matching how the SECURITY-REVIEWER trigger was handled in the same section - and correctly states that manual checklists remain in force until REQ-009 actually lands.
(c) DEPENDS_ON - [REQ-007] still correct. REQ-007 creates the root workspaces array that REQ-009 registers into. The three decision records are not requirements and correctly do not appear.
(d) DESIGN-SYSTEM FIT - not applicable; apps/bot has no UI surface, and REQ-009 explicitly excludes handlers beyond a health path.
(e) SIZE - still one agent turn. The amendment removed the three decision records (the largest writing task in the original) and added one CI step plus one scratch-branch CI round-trip. Net smaller than the version that passed at step-02.

PART 2 ITEM 4 - the two named library-capability claims, spot-checked against real sources.

CLAIM 1 - 0004: grammY's conversations plugin vs PRD FR-3's restart-safe partial writes. OVERSTATED AS WORDED; the decision itself survives. Source: https://grammy.dev/plugins/conversations and the plugin reference. What the plugin actually does: it persists ITS OWN dialogue state - the updates received during the conversation, and the return values of conversation.external() calls - through a pluggable storage adapter (the same adapters the session plugin uses, e.g. FileAdapter). The default backend is an in-memory Map, so restart-survival requires explicitly configuring a persistent adapter; it is not free. The replay engine re-runs the conversation function from the top on each update, which is why side effects must be wrapped in conversation.external(). What it does NOT do is write partial answers into the application's Profile table - that write is application code inside conversation.external(). PRD FR-3 says 'partial answers are written to the Profile row as they arrive'; the plugin gives restart-safe dialogue POSITION, not that. 0004's rationale 1 calls this 'exactly what grammY's conversations plugin exists for' and calls it 'the single strongest reason' - that is an overclaim. The choice is not overturned: the residual substance of rationale 1 (Telegraf requires hand-rolled scene management for the same dialogue state) is real, and rationales 2-4 are unaffected. Filed as ISSUE-1, MINOR.

CLAIM 2 - 0006: Vitest's fake timers make the clock-dependent logic testable. CONFIRMED, with one boundary the record should state. Source: https://vitest.dev/api/vi.html. vi.useFakeTimers() fakes setTimeout/clearTimeout, setInterval/clearInterval, setImmediate/clearImmediate and the Date constructor by default; vi.setSystemTime() moves the simulated clock and affects new Date(), Date.now() and performance.now(); vi.advanceTimersByTime() and advanceTimersByTimeAsync() drive scheduled work. That is precisely what the T-24h promotion halt, the T-3h / T+2h / T+24h jobs and no_show-after-ends_at need - PROVIDED those comparisons happen in JavaScript. The boundary: fake timers do not reach Postgres. A comparison expressed as SQL now() runs on the database clock and is untouched. This matters here specifically because PRD section 5 makes no_show, registration_open and waitlist position computed-not-stored, and 0005's own rationales 2 and 3 actively push that computation toward SQL. The two records therefore interact, and neither says so. Separately, 0006 understates node:test: since Node 20 it has mock.timers.enable({apis:['Date'], now}) with setTime() and tick(), so 'hand-rolled clock injection everywhere' is not accurate - the gap is ergonomic, not a missing capability. Vitest still stands on rationales 2-4 (nothing is published so node:test's dependency-freedom benefit is unrealized; one runner across both workspaces; machine-readable reporters and --run exiting non-zero give TEST-RUNNER real output). Filed as ISSUE-2, MINOR.

PART 2 ITEMS 1-3, PER RECORD.
0004 - fair characterization PASS: two options, and Telegraf's genuine advantages are stated (smaller dependency tree, larger tutorial and StackOverflow corpus). Own cost stated (larger dependency surface, thinner third-party tutorials). It flags grammY's own comparison page as an interested source and says the Telegraf-types criticism was corroborated elsewhere - good practice. Grounding PASS: rationale 2 cites core-directives' weak-model tolerance and rationale 4 cites PRD section 1's 0.06 rps to dismiss Telegraf's serverless advantage as inapplicable here - neither would read identically for another project. No contradiction with 0001-0003, the done requirements (all apps/web-only) or security-invariants.md; the plugin-deferral clause actively protects REQ-009's no-domain-logic boundary.
0005 - the strongest of the three. Fair characterization PASS, and specifically not a strawman of Prisma: it credits Prisma 7's Rust-engine removal and the 14MB-to-1.6MB bundle drop, and it says outright under 'What this costs - stated honestly' that Prisma's shadow-database verification catches a destructive migration Drizzle Kit will happily generate, that this is a genuine loss, and that it is accepted deliberately. It also explicitly discards performance benchmarks as irrelevant at 0.06 rps rather than citing them as support. Grounding PASS: the deciding factor is PRD section 1 and 11's exportability constraint - the platform absorbing this system later - which is project-specific and would not transfer. Reinforces rather than contradicts S6/S7/S8 (database-level invariants) and S13 (the migration sign-off).
0006 - three options named. Fair characterization is the weakest of the three: the node:test treatment is inaccurate on timer mocking (ISSUE-2), and Jest is dismissed in two lines - defensible, since it loses on the stated ESM ground and the record says plainly that it was rejected without further analysis rather than pretending to a full comparison. Own cost stated (adds a dependency and a config file). Grounding PASS: the 'why this can no longer be deferred' table ties each untestable property to a specific PRD section and explains why a manual check fails - entirely project-specific. The closing scope limit (no coverage target, no test-first mandate, because a number invented in the abstract is what this project's directives forbid) is good discipline. No contradiction with 0001-0003 or security-invariants.md.

PART 3 - CONSEQUENTIAL CORRECTNESS. All three consequences are stated somewhere, but only one is stated where it bites. 0006's is wired correctly: the TEST-DESIGNER / TEST-RUNNER change lives in AGENT_SYSTEM.md section 7, which those roles encounter, and the CI change is both in REQ-009's description and in its acceptance criterion 3. 0004's framework-free-domain-logic rule and 0005's SQL-review-plus-S13-sign-off rule are restated in REQ-009's description - but REQ-009 is the one-time skeleton requirement, and both rules actually bind from REQ-010 onward, where the acting agent reads a different handoff and REVIEWER / SECURITY-REVIEWER read their own role files. Per core-directives' weak-model-tolerance rule, a consequence recorded where the acting agent will not read it has not been established. Filed as ISSUE-3, MINOR - the decisions themselves are sound, the wiring is incomplete.

issues.title: 0004 rationale 1 overstates what grammY's conversations plugin persists
issues.detail: docs/agents/decisions/0004-telegram-framework-grammy.md rationale 1 quotes PRD FR-3's 'partial answers are written to the Profile row as they arrive - a restart mid-form loses nothing' and then asserts 'Multi-step stateful dialogue is exactly what grammY's conversations plugin exists for,' calling it the single strongest reason for the choice. Verified against https://grammy.dev/plugins/conversations: the plugin persists its OWN dialogue state (received updates plus conversation.external() return values) via a pluggable storage adapter, and its default backend is an in-memory Map - restart-survival requires explicitly configuring a persistent adapter. It never writes partial answers into the application's Profile table; that write is application code inside conversation.external(), under either framework. The decision is not overturned - the residual substance of rationale 1 (Telegraf needs hand-rolled scene management for the same dialogue state) plus rationales 2-4 carry it - but the record should be amended to say the plugin provides restart-safe dialogue POSITION given a configured persistent adapter, while FR-3's per-field Profile write remains application code. Route to ORCH as the record's author; REQ-VALIDATOR does not rewrite records.

issues.title: 0006 understates node:test's timer mocking, and omits the SQL-clock boundary of fake timers
issues.detail: Two corrections to docs/agents/decisions/0006-test-framework-vitest.md. (i) Option B says node:test's 'time/clock control is more manual' and rationale 1 says choosing it would mean 'hand-rolled clock injection everywhere'. Node has shipped mock.timers.enable({apis:['Date'], now}) with setTime() and tick() since Node 20, so the gap is ergonomic rather than a missing capability - the record's fair-characterization duty is not fully met, though the decision stands on its other rationales. (ii) Rationale 1's fake-timer claim is CONFIRMED for JavaScript-side clock logic (https://vitest.dev/api/vi.html: useFakeTimers fakes Date and the setTimeout/setInterval/setImmediate families; setSystemTime moves new Date() and Date.now(); advanceTimersByTime drives scheduled work) but does not extend to Postgres - a comparison written as SQL now() runs on the database clock, untouched by fake timers. This is load-bearing here because PRD section 5 makes no_show, registration_open and waitlist position computed-not-stored, and 0005's rationales 2 and 3 deliberately push that computation toward SQL. DATA-DESIGNER and BACKEND-DEV need the rule that any time comparison which must be unit-testable takes the current time as an injected parameter rather than calling now() inside SQL. Neither 0005 nor 0006 says this today. Route to ORCH; resolve before REQ-010 is dispatched, since REQ-010 is the schema requirement where it first bites.

issues.title: 0004's and 0005's binding consequences are wired only into REQ-009, which is not where they bite
issues.detail: 0004's framework-free-domain-logic rule and 0005's SQL-review-plus-SECURITY-REVIEWER-S13-sign-off rule are both correctly restated in REQ-009's description - but REQ-009 is the one-time skeleton requirement, and both rules bind from REQ-010 onward, where the acting agent reads a different requirement's handoff and the gating roles read their own role files. Per core-directives.md's weak-model-tolerance rule ('assume the acting agent has no memory of this file's reasoning beyond what is written down'), a consequence recorded where the acting agent will not encounter it has not been established. 0006's equivalent consequence WAS wired correctly, into AGENT_SYSTEM.md section 7 where TEST-DESIGNER and TEST-RUNNER meet it - that is the model to follow. Concretely: REVIEWER's role file should carry 'a domain rule written inside a grammY handler body is a finding', and SECURITY-REVIEWER's role file or security-invariants.md S13 should carry 'a Drizzle Kit-generated migration that drops or rewrites a column holding personal data or attendance history requires sign-off'. This is a wiring gap, not a defect in the decisions. Route to ORCH.

issues.title: REQ-009 acceptance criterion 2 forbids a dependency on node:test, which cannot exist as a dependency
issues.detail: docs/agents/requirements.yaml REQ-009 acceptance criterion 2 ends 'A dependency on Telegraf, Prisma, Jest or node:test is a FAIL, as is any grammY plugin added at this stage.' Telegraf, Prisma and Jest are npm packages and are checkable in package.json. node:test is a Node built-in module and can never appear as a dependency, so that clause is uncheckable as written; the checkable form is 'no test file imports node:test'. This does not make criterion 2 a check-(a) FAIL - the three real package names plus the exact-version rule carry it, and the clause's intent is unambiguous - but it should be fixed at the source rather than left for RELEASE-VALIDATOR to reinterpret. Route to ORCH / REQ-ANALYST.

result.next_action: Return to ORCH. The amended REQ-009 and decisions/0004, 0005 and 0006 all PASS the gate - no FAIL, no MAJOR, no BLOCKER; REQ-009 is eligible for WF-02. Four MINOR issues for ORCH to resolve as the records' author, since REQ-VALIDATOR does not rewrite them: (1) amend 0004's rationale 1 to distinguish restart-safe dialogue position from FR-3's Profile-row partial writes, and to note the plugin's default storage is in-memory; (2) amend 0006 to characterize node:test's mock.timers accurately and to state that fake timers do not reach the database clock, adding the injected-current-time rule that 0005's SQL-leaning rationales make necessary; (3) wire 0004's and 0005's consequences into REVIEWER's and SECURITY-REVIEWER's role files, following how 0006's consequence was wired into AGENT_SYSTEM.md section 7; (4) correct REQ-009 criterion 2's node:test clause to 'no test file imports node:test'. None of the four blocks REQ-009. Issues 2(ii) and 3 should be resolved before REQ-010 is dispatched, because REQ-010 is the schema requirement where both first bite.
